subject: Startups
title: Slack's Bottom-Up Adoption
description: A micro-lesson that makes Slack's Bottom-Up Adoption usable.

hook.text: Slack didn't sell to CEOs. It sold to individual teams. One team tried it, then the whole company switched.

buildup.text: A single engineer would set up Slack for a small team. Others saw it working and asked to join.

discovery.text: IT departments found Shadow Slack installations everywhere. By the time they noticed, adoption was unstoppable.

twist.text: Traditional enterprise sales is top-down: pitch the CEO. Slack inverted it. Users demanded it from the bottom up.

climax.text: Slack reached $1 billion in annual revenue faster than almost any SaaS company. Grassroots adoption drove it.

punchline.text: Win the users first. Management follows.

quiz.question: How did Slack typically enter large organizations?
